original_value: Although the last two decades have seen an increasing number of activity recognition applications with wearable devices, there is still a lack of tools specifically designed to support their development. The development of activity recognition algorithms for wearable devices is particularly challenging because of the several requirements that have to be met simultaneously (e.g., low energy consumption, small and lightweight, accurate recognition). Activity recognition applications are usually developed in a series of iterations to annotate sensor data and to analyze, develop and assess the performance of a recognition algorithm. This paper presents the Wearables Development Toolkit, an Integrated Development Environment designed to lower the entrance barrier to the development of activity recognition applications with wearables. It specifically focuses on activity recognition using on-body inertial sensors. The toolkit offers a repository of high-level reusable components and a set of tools with functionality to annotate data, to analyze and develop activity recognition algorithms and to assess their recognition and computational performance. We demonstrate the versatility of the toolkit with three applications and describe how we developed it incrementally based on two user studies.

result.paraphrase: Although wearable activity recognition has grown substantially over the past twenty years, there remains a shortage of tools purpose-built to aid its development. Building activity recognition algorithms for wearables is especially difficult because several requirements must be satisfied at once, such as low power use, compact and lightweight design, and accurate recognition. These applications are typically created through repeated iterations to annotate sensor data and to analyze, develop, and evaluate the performance of a recognition algorithm. This paper introduces the Wearables Development Toolkit, an integrated development environment intended to reduce the barrier to entry for developing wearable activity recognition applications. It is specifically focused on activity recognition with on-body inertial sensors. The toolkit provides a repository of reusable high-level components and a suite of tools for annotating data, analyzing and developing activity recognition algorithms, and assessing both recognition and computational performance. We show the toolkit’s versatility through three applications and explain how it was developed incrementally on the basis of two user studies.
